thread:
alex: Heads-up: noticed a small perf regression on prod after the new execution-path selector went live — ~3% p99 increase for short sequences (<=32). cpu/GPU utilization looks fine.

maria: thanks for flagging. which model & variant? GQA or MQA path?

alex: gpt-4o-ish test profile, MQA enabled. selector now picks an "op_chain" that prefers fused-batched kernels for medium seqlen, and falls back to paged-attn for long ones. I suspect the fallbacks or KV layout interaction.

cheng: can you paste the selector rule snippet and a perf trace? also pinging @perf-bot for flamegraphs :eyes: 

alex:
```
# simplified rule
if tokens <= 64 and mqa_shards > 1:
  choose: fused_mqa_batched_v2
elif tokens <= 128:
  choose: fused_mqa_batched_v1
else:
  choose: paged_attn_blocked
```

alex: perf-bot output (end-to-end p99): baseline(older picker)=78ms, new=80.5ms. token dist skew: 70% <=32 tokens, 20% 33-96, 10% >96.

perf-bot: flame: top hotpaths -> kv_cache_copy (18%), small-kernel-launch (22%), attention_block_dispatch (26%). No obvious device mem stalls.

maria: kv_cache_copy at 18% is interesting. Did the KV layout change between versions? New layout uses 256B microblocks (blocksz=256) vs old 128B.

alex: yes, we switched to 256 to reduce pointer overhead for large seqlen. Might hurt short sequences due to extra memcpy.

cheng: hypothesis: for short seqlen + MQA we lose because fused_mqa_batched_v2 expects denser kv stripe packing. With larger microblocks we do extra padding and extra memcpy per request.

maria: can you try two quick probes on staging: (A) force selector to pick fused_mqa_batched_v1 for tokens<=32, (B) revert kv microblock size to 128 for that deployment. microbench each for 1h.

alex: started probe A at 2040012400. microbench results so far (5m windows): A median=12.1ms, p99=19.3ms. Baseline (old picker + 128B) had p99=18.7ms. New rollout p99 was 20.0ms. So probe A helps a bit.

cheng: good. try B next. Also run `nvprof`-style capture for small kernel launches to see launch overhead vs memcpy.

alex: started probe B at 2040012620 (kv microblock=128). Initial 10m aggregate: median=11.9ms, p99=18.6ms — matches baseline. KV copy hotspot dropped to ~10%.

maria: looks like kv microblock size change regresses short seqs. We need a selector that is layout-aware: pick a path that avoids extra memcopies when microblock>128 or choose different blocksz by seqlen.

cheng: proposal: autotune table keyed by (device arch, mqa_shards, kv_microblock, avg_seq_bucket). Add a fallback to leaner fused kernel for short seq when microblock>=256. Also consider async memcpy batching across requests (prefix cache coalescing).

alex: agree. I'll open a small RFC and a follow-up experiment to test async coalesce. Also tagging @sre-bot to schedule a canary rollback plan if we flip the default block size.

sre-bot: Canary window scheduled: 2040016000 - 2040020000. Will auto-rollback on error-rate or p99>baseline+5%.

maria: thanks — next steps: 1) RFC for layout-aware selector (alex), 2) perf autotune table prototype (cheng), 3) short-term revert candidate (alex). Keep notes here.

alex: adding brief checklist to the thread:
- [x] reproduce locally
- [x] run probe A (selector tweak)
- [x] run probe B (kv blocksz revert)
- [ ] draft RFC
- [ ] implement autotune table

cheng: also capture a small kernel timeline using `nvtx` ranges for the next probe. helps quantify async memcpy gains.

alex: will attach traces in the RFC. thanks all.
